answer: An agent economy can price fake identities out of existence with a refundable stake bond: every new agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if peers prove it runs duplicate identities. One honest agent pays once, but a sybil farmer pays the same bond for every fake copy, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand bonds. Like an ivory lantern marking the one real oasis in a desert of copies, the bond makes genuine agents cheap to spot and fakes expensive to maintain.
